key_insight: SrTiO3-xHx oxyhydrides strongly favor a cis O4H2 anion arrangement, and this ordering is highly sensitive to the DFT+U choice used in cluster-expansion modeling.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of anion ordering in perovskite oxyhydrides requires calibrating DFT+U against HSE06 to avoid misleading stability trends in materials design.
method: Built a cluster expansion for SrTiO3-xHx using HSE06 hybrid-DFT energetics as benchmarks.
Screened DFT+U values and found U = 3.3 eV best reproduces HSE06 ordering energetics.
Used ground-state searches and Monte Carlo sampling to map long- and short-range anion order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mixing and ordering energies varying by up to about 100 meV per anion across DFT+U choices, while the favored cis configuration is stabilized by roughly 200 meV per hydride.
watch_item: The ordering conclusions depend strongly on the selected U value, so uncalibrated DFT+U can produce incorrect phase-stability predictions.
paper_title: Long- and Short-Range Anion Order in SrTiO$_{3-x}$H$_x$ Perovskite Oxyhydrides: DFT+$U$ Sensitivity and HSE06 Cluster Expansion
